tools.name: search_workspace
tools.description: Search the learner's sources for passages matching one focused query.

file_ids.description: Restrict to these workspace items (ids from list_sources); only source files and notes hold text to search. Omit to search the current scope.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: List the workspace's source files and study materials by chapter, with ids, kinds, editability and passage counts.

tools.name: search_files_summary
tools.description: Find the user's files and materials by their names and summaries, in their workspaces and with no workspace. Each hit gives its id, workspace and chapter (or no workspace), whether the user can edit it, and its summary when it has one. Use it before search_files_content.

tools.name: search_files_content
tools.description: Search the content of the user's files, in their workspaces and with no workspace, for passages matching one focused query. Each passage names its file's workspace and chapter and whether the user can edit it.

file_ids.description: Restrict to these items (ids from search_files_summary or list_files); only files and notes hold text to search. Omit to search all of them.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List one of the user's workspaces by chapter (workspace_id), or without it their newest files and materials with no workspace, with ids, kinds and whether the user can edit each.

workspace_id.description: A workspace id from search_files_summary, search_files_content or a read; omit it to list the files with no workspace.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Create a workspace of the user's own, only when they asked for one. Every field is optional: without a name it is New Workspace (n). A name, description or tag over its limit is cut to it and saved.

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: Read a source file or note in order from a chunk index: a passage's surrounding argument, or a short document end to end.

tools.name: capture_page
tools.description: Render a PDF page a shown passage cites, or a region of it, as an image you read directly. An uploaded image is page 1. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files have no pages here: inspect_office_document reads them, pictures included.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] on a 0-1000 page grid, top-left origin, to zoom into a table, figure or formula.

tools.name: read_study_progress
tools.description: Read the learner's study progress in this workspace: files and materials done or started, recent quiz results, and the chapters they retain least.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the shared library of verified textbook excerpts, one section of one book each. A hit is a selection aid; read_knowledge reads the excerpt.

subject.description: A subject id listed below: search only its excerpts.

tools.name: read_knowledge
tools.description: Read an excerpt's reviewed notes and source chunks in order from a chunk index; the notes and scope come on its first page.

tools.name: capture_knowledge_page
tools.description: Render a printed page an excerpt covers, or a region of it, as an image you read directly.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] on a 0-1000 page grid, top-left origin, to zoom into a table, figure or formula.

tools.name: search_web
tools.description: Search the web. Expensive: each search costs the learner credits, so call it only when the workspace, the library and your own knowledge cannot answer (recent events, facts they lack). At most 3 searches per learner message, one focused query each, written in your own words rather than copied from the learner's files. Results are pages anyone can publish.

query.description: One focused query. site:, -site:, lang:, after: and before: narrow it.

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Read a skill: the full instructions for one kind of work, listed below with when to read it. Read it before that work.

tools.name: create_material
tools.description: Create a study material from content you wrote, in the formats the editing skill describes (a note: the note_building skill). A quiz is made with add_questions.

chapter_id.description: The chapter to file it in; omit to leave it unfiled.

excerpt_ids.description: Library excerpts it was written from; they become its attribution. Optional; omitted, the excerpts read since your last write are credited.

sources.description: The made-from line: each source it is made from, named in words or by id: workspace files, notes, Office files, quizzes and flashcard sets (ids from list_sources), or outside sources such as a lecture, a handout or a web address. At most 20, each at most 200 characters. An id or exact name of a workspace item is stored as that item's current name. Omit it to name none.

tools.name: add_questions
tools.description: Add questions to a quiz (quiz_id), or create a quiz with them (title); read the editing skill before the first call. A question's fields make its kind: multiple choice (options, one correct) and short answer (accepted) are 1 mark each; an open question, answered in writing, has marks and a markscheme adding up to them, and optionally a model_answer. Options are shown shuffled: never refer to one by its letter or position (A, B, "the first", "all of the above"). The result lists each question's id. Example: {"title": "Osmosis", "questions": [{"question": "Which way does water move when a red blood cell is put in pure water?", "options": ["Into the cell", "Out of the cell"], "correct": "Into the cell", "explanation": "From the higher water potential outside."}, {"question": "What percentage of NaCl is normal saline?", "accepted": ["0.9"], "unit": "%"}, {"question": "Explain why the cell bursts.", "marks": 2, "markscheme": [{"text": "Water enters by osmosis", "marks": 1}, {"text": "No cell wall resists the swelling", "marks": 1}], "model_answer": "Water enters by osmosis and, with no cell wall to resist it, the membrane ruptures."}]}

after_question_id.description: Add after this question, not at the end.

chapter_id.description: With title: the new quiz's chapter.

excerpt_ids.description: Library excerpts the questions were written from. Optional; omitted, the excerpts read since your last write are credited.

correct.description: Multiple choice: the one correct option, copied exactly.

explanation.description: Optional: why the answer is right or the worked solution, shown after checking.

hints.description: Open, optional: nudges the learner may open.

markscheme.description: Open: what earns marks, the items' marks adding up to marks.

question.description: The question as the learner reads it.

replaces.description: A question of the quiz to rewrite in place instead (its media is dropped).

unit.description: Short answer to a quantity: the unit shown after the box; accepted then holds plain numbers only, like "9.8".

quiz_id.description: The quiz to add to, a note's quiz too; add_questions' result gives a new quiz's id.

sources.description: With title: the new quiz's made-from line: each source it is made from, named in words or by id: workspace files, notes, Office files, quizzes and flashcard sets (ids from list_sources), or outside sources such as a lecture, a handout or a web address. At most 20, each at most 200 characters. An id or exact name of a workspace item is stored as that item's current name. Omit it to name none.

title.description: Instead of quiz_id: create a quiz with this title.

tools.name: add_question_media
tools.description: Add a chart, a plot or a library figure to one quiz question, shown after its text. A figure is one read_knowledge listed this turn: {"type": "figure", "id": "<figure id>", "caption": "what it shows"}; the question shows it with its printed credit and the quiz credits its book. Example: {"quiz_id": "mat_1", "question_id": "q_3f9a1c2b7e", "media": {"type": "plot", "title": "Action potential", "xTitle": "Time (ms)", "yTitle": "Membrane potential (mV)", "series": [{"name": "Vm", "points": [[0, -70], [1, 30], [2, -80], [4, -70]]}]}}

excerpt_ids.description: Library excerpts the media was drawn from. Optional; omitted, the excerpts read since your last write are credited.

media.description: A note's chart or plot fence JSON, or a library figure.

tools.name: create_deck
tools.description: Create a slide deck from an outline, one title and brief per slide, as the deck skill describes.

chapter_id.description: The chapter to file the deck in; omit to leave it unfiled.

excerpt_ids.description: Library excerpts this was written from; they become the deck's Sources slide. Optional; omitted, the excerpts read since your last write are credited.

sources.description: The made-from line: each source it is made from, named in words or by id: workspace files, notes, Office files, quizzes and flashcard sets (ids from list_sources), or outside sources such as a lecture, a handout or a web address. At most 20, each at most 200 characters. An id or exact name of a workspace item is stored as that item's current name. Omit it to name none.

tools.name: write_slide
tools.description: Write one slide of a deck as SVG in the deck skill's rules; writing a slide again replaces it.

excerpt_ids.description: Library excerpts this was written from; they become the deck's Sources slide. Optional; omitted, the excerpts read since your last write are credited.

tools.name: resolve_source_change
tools.description: Resolve an exact pending-change placeholder. For a file's image change give file_id, change_id and checkpoint: the image is attached to the next message. For a note's data change give material_id and block_id: the block's text before and after is returned. Only use identifiers supplied in the pending-source evidence.

tools.name: inspect_document
tools.description: Read a document's current content as editable targets with stable ids. Inspect before editing; never take edit positions from search results. A quiz's answers, solutions and marking schemes appear only when the user may edit it.

tools.name: edit_document
tools.description: Edit the content of one inspected document: each command names a target and the exact text or value it expects, and one stale expectation refuses the whole call. Edits save directly; replace_block rewrites a note block with formatting or math, and a Mermaid block a learner added as one ```mermaid fence, expecting the source inspect shows as its text. Any note block may be removed or replaced, media included; the only media an edit adds are library figures. A block rewritten as one of its own type keeps its caption and width (a diagram its theme too); an image swapped for a different picture or figure takes the new one's caption. PDFs cannot be edited. Quiz questions are added and replaced with the question tools.

expected_text.description: Exact text to replace as inspect_document shows it, without math; must occur once in the target.

target_id.description: The note block's id; omit for a plain text source.

text.description: Plain replacement text; empty deletes the expected text.

expected_text.description: The block's current text as inspect_document shows it.

markdown.description: The block's new content as note markdown in the note_building skill's format.

after_block_id.description: Insert after this block; "end" appends after the last block, null inserts at the start.

markdown.description: Note markdown in the note_building skill's format.

expected_text.description: The block's current text as inspect_document shows it.

card_id.description: A side left out stays as it is.

expected_back.description: The card's back as inspect_document shows it; required with back.

expected_front.description: The card's front as inspect_document shows it; required with front.

excerpt_ids.description: Library excerpts the added content was written from. Optional; omitted, the excerpts read since your last write are credited.

tools.name: trash_file
tools.description: Move a source file or study material in this workspace to the trash. Only call this when the user asked to delete or remove it. The owner can restore it from Files › Trash within 30 days.

target.description: The file or material to trash.

tools.name: list_trashed_files
tools.description: List the trashed source files and study materials of this workspace with their ids, names and expiry. Use it before restore_file so you never guess an id.

tools.name: restore_file
tools.description: Restore a trashed source file or study material of this workspace. Only call this when the user asked for it; use list_trashed_files to find the id.

target.description: The trashed file or material to restore.

tools.name: inspect_office_document
tools.description: Read a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file as editable targets, as the office_building skill describes. XLSX: without range, its sheets (id, name, used range); with sheet and range, each cell's input and shown value, at most 2,000 cells a read. DOCX: count paragraphs from start with their target ids, styles, lists and table cells, the body's and then the headers', footers' and notes', which take replace_text only; the first page also lists the file's paragraph styles. PPTX: without slide, count slides from start with their layouts and first shapes (id, kind, first line), the first page also listing the deck's layouts; with slide, count of that slide's shapes and paragraphs from start, each shape followed by its paragraphs with their target ids, the first page also giving the slide's speaker notes. Reads also list pictures, charts with their first points, equations and drawn shapes' text. The cheap read: with ids, the pictures come back as images and the charts with every point.

count.description: DOCX: paragraphs to read; PPTX: slides, or with slide shapes and paragraphs.

ids.description: Any format, at most 4: pictures' and charts' ids from an earlier read, copied whole; a picture comes back as an image, a chart with every point. The other arguments are then ignored.

range.description: XLSX: an A1 range on that sheet, like "A1:H40".

sheet.description: XLSX: the sheet's id or name.

start.description: DOCX: first paragraph; PPTX: first slide, or with slide its first shape or paragraph; counting from 0.

tools.name: edit_office_document
tools.description: Edit one Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, or create a Word or Excel file, with the commands of its format as the office_building skill describes. Each command names what it expects as inspect_office_document shows it, and one stale expectation refuses the whole call. Edits save directly. A call's commands are at most 256 KB; a larger call is refused. A call applies at most 50 commands and, per format, DOCX: 20 text replacements, 20 inserted paragraphs, 20 deleted paragraphs, 400 table cells inserted, 5 tables deleted, 30 formatted spans and 200 paragraphs given a list or an alignment; PPTX: 20 text replacements, 20 inserted paragraphs, 20 deleted paragraphs, 30 formatted spans, 200 paragraphs given an alignment, 500 paragraphs of shape and text box text, 50,000 characters of shape and text box text, 20 slides added, 20 slides deleted, 50 slides moved and 20 text boxes added; XLSX: 10,000 cells written, 1,000 inserted rows and columns and 5 sheets added, renamed or deleted. Commands apply in order up to the first that would pass a limit; the rest come back unapplied, by index, to send in another call.

oneOf.description: First command only, without file_id: makes a new file; the call's other commands then apply to it.

chapter_id.description: The chapter to file it in; omit to leave it unfiled.

title.description: The file's name, without its extension.

oneOf.description: XLSX: write a rectangle of cells.

expected.description: The range's current inputs as inspect_office_document shows them, one row per array; "" for an empty cell.

range.description: An A1 range on that sheet, like "B2:D9".

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

values.description: The new inputs as typed, in the range's shape: "=..." for a formula, "" to clear.

oneOf.description: XLSX: format a range; fields left out stay as they are.

number_format.description: automatic, plain_text, number, percent, scientific, currency, date, time, or an Excel number format pattern like "0.0%" or "yyyy-mm-dd".

range.description: An A1 range on that sheet, like "B2:D9".

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

wrap.description: true wraps text inside the cell; false lets it overflow.

oneOf.description: XLSX: add an empty sheet.

after.description: The sheet it follows; omit to add it last.

oneOf.description: XLSX: rename a sheet.

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

oneOf.description: XLSX: insert empty rows.

at.description: The row number the first new row takes; rows from there move down.

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

oneOf.description: XLSX: delete whole rows.

at.description: The first row number to delete.

expected.description: The rows' current inputs as inspect_office_document shows them, one array per row with its cells from column A; trailing empty cells and rows may be left out, [] for empty rows.

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

oneOf.description: XLSX: insert empty columns.

at.description: The column letter the first new column takes, like "C"; columns from there move right.

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

oneOf.description: XLSX: delete whole columns.

at.description: The first column letter to delete, like "C".

expected.description: The columns' current inputs as inspect_office_document shows them, one array per row from row 1 holding the deleted columns' cells; trailing empty cells and rows may be left out, [] for empty columns.

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

oneOf.description: XLSX: delete a sheet.

sheet.description: The sheet's id or name as inspect_office_document lists it.

oneOf.description: DOCX, PPTX: replace text inside one paragraph or shape.

expected_text.description: Exact text to replace as inspect_office_document shows it; must occur once in the target.

target_id.description: The paragraph's or shape's target id from inspect_office_document.

text.description: Plain replacement text; empty deletes the expected text.

oneOf.description: DOCX, PPTX: insert one paragraph right after after_id or right before before_id (at most one); DOCX paragraphs go in the document body, at its end with neither.

after_id.description: The paragraph it follows, a target id from inspect_office_document.

before_id.description: The paragraph it precedes; the first paragraph's id inserts at the start.

list.description: DOCX: start or end a list; omit to continue the paragraph before it.

style.description: DOCX: a paragraph style id inspect_office_document lists; omit to continue the paragraph before it as Enter does.

text.description: One paragraph's plain text, up to 5,000 characters, without line breaks.

oneOf.description: DOCX, PPTX: delete one paragraph, never its story's or shape's last.

expected_text.description: The paragraph's whole text as inspect_office_document shows it.

target_id.description: The paragraph's target id from inspect_office_document.

oneOf.description: DOCX: make paragraphs bulleted or numbered, or end their list.
DOCX: add a table of text to the document body, followed by an empty paragraph.

after_id.description: The body paragraph it follows; several inserts after one paragraph keep their order. Omit to add it at the end of the document.

rows.description: The cells' text, one array per row, every row the same length; at most 20 rows of 10 cells.

oneOf.description: DOCX: delete a table.

expected.description: The table's cells' text as inspect_office_document shows them, one array per row; a cell's paragraphs joined by line breaks.

oneOf.description: DOCX, PPTX: format text inside one paragraph; fields left out stay as they are.

target_id.description: A paragraph's target id from inspect_office_document.

text.description: The exact text to format as inspect_office_document shows it; must occur once in the paragraph.

oneOf.description: DOCX, PPTX: align one paragraph.

target_id.description: A paragraph's target id from inspect_office_document.

oneOf.description: PPTX: replace a shape's whole text; its paragraphs keep their level and bullet, added ones continue the last.

expected_text.description: The shape's whole text as the slide read shows it, its paragraphs joined by line breaks.

paragraphs.description: The new text, one string a paragraph without line breaks; [""] empties the shape. At most 50 paragraphs and 5,000 characters together.

shape_id.description: The shape's id from inspect_office_document's slide read.

oneOf.description: PPTX: add a slide with its layout's title and text placeholders, empty, right after after_slide or right before before_slide (at most one), last with neither.

layout.description: A layout id the deck read lists; omit for the layout of the slide it follows (the first slide's when it goes first).

oneOf.description: PPTX: delete a slide, never the deck's only one.

expected_text.description: The slide's text as its slide read shows it: every paragraph, one a line, in shape order, then its speaker notes as the read shows them (cut marker included); blank lines and the spaces around a line are not compared.

oneOf.description: PPTX: move a slide right after after_slide or right before before_slide (exactly one).
PPTX: add a text box to a slide, its box in points from the slide's top left corner, inside the slide.

paragraphs.description: The text, one string a paragraph without line breaks. At most 50 paragraphs and 5,000 characters together.

x.description: Points from the slide's left or top edge.

y.description: Points from the slide's left or top edge.

file_id.description: The file to edit; omit when the first command is create.

formats.note: Markdown. A note may also hold, where they help an idea: ```chart fences comparing labelled categories, JSON {"type": "chart", "kind": "bar"|"hbar"|"line"|"area"|"pie"|"stacked", "title", "labels": [...], "series": [{"name", "values": one number per label}]} with any unit in the title; ```plot fences for numbers against numbers: curves of a quantity along a numeric axis (a membrane potential over time, a titration curve) or a scatter of points, JSON {"type": "plot", "kind"?: "line"|"scatter" (default line), "title", "xTitle", "yTitle" (axis names with units), "series": 1 to 4 [{"name", "points": [[x, y], ...] in x order for a line, 2 to 60 (1 or more for a scatter)}], "lines"?: [{"axis": "x"|"y", "value", "label"?}] dashed reference lines, "marks"?: [{"x", "y", "label"}] labelled points}; ```quiz fences (YAML `questions:` list, each a question as add_questions takes it) and ```flashcards fences (YAML `cards:` list of `front`/`back`), each a knowledge check sized and placed as the study preferences say; and ```html-embed fences for an interactive (YAML: a quoted `caption`, `html: |`), at most 10 per note. The html is one small snippet under 64 KB: inline CSS and script; a library may load (script src, stylesheet link or module import) only from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net, https://esm.sh or https://unpkg.com at an exact version, and nothing else reaches the network (no other src or href, no fetch, no navigating the page); colours only from the provided variables --bg, --fg, --muted, --accent and --border so it follows the light and dark theme, height fitting its content with no vh or vw units. The frame already gives the body the page's font (--font), text colour, no margin and a transparent background, and form controls the accent colour, so style only what differs. Use an interactive only where moving something teaches more than a still picture.
